questions.question_text: What is the equation of the $yz$-plane?

options.why: Named the plane after an axis lying in it, rather than the axis perpendicular to it.
Gave the equation of the flat $xy$-plane instead.

questions.solution_text:
The $yz$-plane contains the $y$-axis and the $z$-axis, so every point on it has no movement in the $x$ direction.
$x=0$

questions.question_text: A point lies on the $z$-axis, $7$ units below the origin. What are its coordinates?

options.why: Put the value in the $y$ slot, which belongs to the $y$-axis rather than the $z$-axis.
Placed the value in the right slot but ignored that below the origin means a negative $z$.
Used the wrong slot and also ignored that below the origin means a negative value.

questions.solution_text:
A point on the $z$-axis has $x=0$ and $y=0$.
Below the origin means $z$ is negative.
$(0,0,-7)$

questions.question_text: Which of these points lies in the same octant as $(-5,-2,6)$?

options.why: Reversed every sign, which gives the octant directly opposite through the origin.
Matched the first and third signs but ignored that the $y$-coordinate must also be negative.
Kept the same three numbers but in a different order, which changes which coordinate carries each sign.

questions.solution_text:
$(-5,-2,6)$ has signs $-$, $-$, $+$.
$(-1,-3,4)$ has signs $-$, $-$, $+$.
The signs match in all three coordinates, so $(-1,-3,4)$ lies in the same octant.

questions.question_text: How far is the point $A(8,-4,3)$ from the $xz$-plane?

options.why: Used the $x$-coordinate, which gives the distance to the $yz$-plane instead.
Used the $z$-coordinate, which gives the distance to the $xy$-plane instead.
Chose the right coordinate but did not take its size, so the answer came out negative.

questions.solution_text:
The $xz$-plane is $y=0$, so the distance is the size of the $y$-coordinate.
$|-4|$
$=4$ units

questions.question_text: The point $B(3,\,2k+8,\,-1)$ lies on the $xz$-plane. What is the value of $k$?

options.why: Solved $2k=8$ instead of $2k=-8$, losing the sign when moving $8$ across.
Ignored the coefficient $2$ and solved $k+8=0$.
Set $k$ itself to zero rather than setting the $y$-coordinate to zero.

questions.question_text: A point $P$ lies on the negative side of the $yz$-plane, on the positive side of the $xz$-plane, and below the $xy$-plane. Which of the following could be the coordinates of $P$?

options.why: Associated the $yz$-plane with $y$ and the $xz$-plane with $x$, swapping the signs of the first two coordinates.
Identified the signs of $x$ and $y$ correctly but treated being below the $xy$-plane as a positive $z$-coordinate.
Swapped the $x$ and $y$ plane conditions and also treated being below the $xy$-plane as positive $z$.

questions.solution_text:
The $yz$-plane is $x=0$, so lying on the negative side means $x < 0$.
The $xz$-plane is $y=0$, so lying on the positive side means $y > 0$.
The $xy$-plane is $z=0$, so lying below the plane means $z < 0$.
The signs must be $(-, +, -)$, which matches $(-5, 8, -2)$.
